scope: Phase four: 2D curves, Copy/Delete/Save/Replace dependencies and LOD value editing
status: Implemented and validated on macOS arm64 Release; final-source paired timing and same-program control pass. Phase four remains in progress.
implemented: Specialized parameters reuse the existing C interface version 12, owned records, real lists and integer lists. No public STL, SDK, SDL or ImGui types or new value-owner handles are added.

2D curve values include fitting, point flags, positions, TCB and explicit tangents. The core keeps derived data privately for exact history restoration; owned SDK subclasses expose protected storage without downcasting SDK objects or reimplementing the file format.

A complete edit is normalized by one native batch update. History restores prepared native data directly, preserving tangent rounding, length and evaluation. Native copies use already described data without applying editor-only creation rules; empty legacy curves and exact copied curve bytes are covered.

Curve preview evaluation uses a registered query and the existing bounded query cache. It matches native evaluation and does not change the source. Native layout, point selection/drag/add/remove, linear toggle, grid/tangent controls and compact preview are preserved.

All four dependency operations expose owned mode and option arrays plus native class/option metadata. Changing modes preserves unknown class slots and hidden option bits. Class selection/folding and the native tree layout remain presentation state.
LOD retains flags and all six proportions, including hidden values, and keeps the existing animation/mesh/patch/alpha and percent controls.

The native curve, dependency and LOD drawing/write branches, duplicate dependency editor and parallel row values are removed. ParameterBox uses the selected query, renderer and modifier through its existing working copy. Nested values submit one parent edit and retain member identity.

Curve/dependency presentation state uses fixed keys in its ImGui window. Full document/object/lifetime fields reset state on target changes; dialog working copies keep their state while native work pauses drawing. Inline reappearance resets selection without allocating keys for every new working copy.

Held-value copying now restores the carrier pointer and destroys the carrier after exceptions, and reports native copy failure. A copy that writes and throws or silently refuses is compensated without leaking objects.

Independent module providers replace the specialized query, renderer and modifier. Open dialogs retain the captured choices after configuration changes. The module descriptor arrays now use owned vectors and derive their published counts from those vectors.

Opaque plugin storage still uses the existing native copier/state path. Its regression now registers an opaque curve-storage type so the test continues exercising that path after ordinary curves become describable.
SDK sources, existing SDK patches/untracked files, file formats and GPU viewport rendering/transfer implementation are unchanged.
Editing Y does not clamp an untouched legacy X outside 0..1. X bounds are applied only when X is edited; a native UI regression preserves the original coordinate.

checks.core_cases: Forty draft updates before one commit; cancellation/no-change retaining Dirty and Redo; curve fitting, explicit tangents, repeated byte-exact undo/redo, length/GetPos restoration, native preview equality, finite/shape/count bounds, exact native copy and empty legacy curve copy; all four dependency modes retaining hidden slots/bits; throwing and refusing dependency copiers with carrier counts unchanged; LOD hidden flags/proportions; one nested parent edit retaining native members. The inline curve regression also covers reappearance and editing Y while retaining a legacy X outside the usual range.

initial_failed_checks.reason: The new test expected EDITOR_NO_CHANGE directly from FinishEdit, which queues accepted edits. Corrected to check the queued result and unchanged history afterward.

The test assumed every dependency operation has visible native options. Save/Replace may have none; Copy/Delete require their native options while all four operations still verify stored data preservation.
The UI selector does not accept the supplied regex alternation. The actual module suite was run instead, including all new cases.

checks.native_cleanup: The previously recorded file-menu cleanup crashes did not occur in these complete runs. No root cause or native cleanup fix is claimed.

performance.scope: Unchanged cubes64 Release editor-frame benchmark, eleven paired groups, at least fifteen seconds warmup and one second per group. No builds or CTest suites ran during capture.
performance.reference_preparation: Before editing, git archive froze df3101f sources and the existing built program/runtime libraries were copied into out/phase-four-special/reference-build. CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY in the copied metadata identifies the frozen source. The launcher source_revision describes the active repository; source and binary hashes identify the measured programs.
performance.sdk_change_option: --sdk-change only permits the pre-existing dirty SDK. This batch makes no SDK change; recursive source/untracked fingerprints and both sets of twenty-two runtime hashes are equal.
performance.result: Final-source paired comparison and subsequent same-program control both pass the original 3% limits. Earlier failed and passing captures from the previous source version are retained. No thresholds, benchmark source or capture were replaced.
performance.stable_counters: Readbacks, uploads, target creations/releases and path selections are zero. One explicit verification readback occurs outside timing.
